headline: High: Flowise’s shared server datastore and broad file/network access create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when paired with opik’s REST-facing observability path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and uses tools as nodes, while opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress. A shared filesystem or API-fed workflow can let attacker-controlled content from one side be treated as instructions by the other. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Flowise workflows ingest files or API responses from opik without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF opik REST payloads are rendered into Flowise prompts or tool inputs, attacker-controlled text can steer execution.
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all cross-agent payloads.
Reject instruction-like text from opik before Flowise prompt assembly.
Use a read-only handoff directory for shared files.
Require explicit human approval for any tool-using Flowise node fed by opik output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and its shared state is via server datastore; opik has broad network egress and a REST API. If sensitive chatflow data is passed into opik, either agent could expose it beyond the intended boundary. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF chatflow inputs or uploaded files contain secrets and are forwarded to opik REST endpoints, leakage occurs.
IF Flowise server datastore is shared across instances and opik can read from that store, cross-tenant exposure is possible.
mitigations: Disable forwarding of raw prompts and file contents to opik.
Store secrets outside Flowise-managed files.
Restrict opik API access to a dedicated service account.
Turn on redaction for chatflow logs and traces.
Separate per-tenant storage namespaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress; opik has broad network egress and REST API access. Even without explicit write access in opik’s profile, both can mutate shared external resources through APIs or files if orchestrated together. Because opik’s write surface is under-specified, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same mutable REST resource, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Flowise writes files that opik also reads or updates, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces per agent.
Add optimistic locking or version checks on shared records.
Make Flowise outputs append-only where possible.
Serialize writes through one coordinator service.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can pass outputs between nodes, and opik exposes a REST API for evaluation/observability. If Flowise output is treated as authoritative input to opik without verification, errors can cascade into downstream reports or actions. The pairwise interaction is inferred, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF opik consumes Flowise-generated facts without validation, hallucinations can propagate.
IF Flowise routes model output directly into opik workflows, a single bad node can contaminate downstream results.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before opik ingestion.
Require schema validation on Flowise outputs.
Flag low-confidence fields for human review.
Keep opik evaluation separate from action-taking workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention constraints. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while opik’s profile lists no data classes touched. With no documented mismatch, only a low compliance risk is visible, and the other agent is not cited because no specific opik compliance boundary is stated.
conditions: IF deployment policy requires a specific residency or retention regime not enforced by Flowise, compliance gaps can appear.
IF chatflow data includes regulated content and opik stores it outside the required jurisdiction, a mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed through both systems.
Disable storage of regulated content in shared traces.
Set retention limits on Flowise logs and opik records.
Review jurisdiction and DPA requirements before enabling cross-system logging.
